definitions.success: A play is a success if it gains 40% of the yards to go on 1st down, 60% on 2nd down, and all of them on 3rd or 4th down. A touchdown always counts.
definitions.explosive: An explosive play is a pass of 20+ yards or a run of 10+ yards.
definitions.garbage: Garbage time is when a game is so lopsided that the result is settled and teams play differently: a lead of more than 38 points in the 1st quarter, 28 in the 2nd, 22 in the 3rd or 16 in the 4th. Overtime is never garbage time.
definitions.efficiency: Efficiency (EPA per play) measures how much each play changes a team's expected scoring on the drive. Above zero helps the offense; the NFL data includes it and college data does not, so college shows success rate instead.
definitions.pass: Pass plays are dropbacks: completions, incompletions, interceptions and sacks (a sack counts as a pass play for the yards it lost).
definitions.rush: Rushes are designed runs and scrambles. Kneel-downs, spikes, two-point tries and plays nullified by penalty are not counted anywhere.
definitions.drive: A drive is one possession. Offensive touchdowns are separate from touchdowns scored by the defense or special teams against that offense, which end the drive as a score for the other side.
definitions.redzone: A red-zone trip is a drive that reached the opponent's 20-yard line or closer.
definitions.opportunity: A scoring opportunity is a drive that reached the opponent's 40-yard line or closer.
definitions.afterTurnover: Points after a takeaway are the offensive points scored on the drive that began with the interception or fumble recovery. They are not all caused by the turnover: a team given a short field might have scored anyway.
